findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key are no longer serialized
findings.body: BuildIndex now only holds cacheMu while inserting the finished index, and GetIndex uses a short RLock that returns nil while another goroutine is still building. Two concurrent getOrCreateIndex/Search/init calls for the same NamespacedResource can therefore both invoke BuildIndex, both call bleve.New/NewMemOnly (for file-backed indexes, both on the same directory path), both run the expensive builder, and then overwrite each other in b.cache. The losing bleve index is never closed, leaking file handles/directory locks, and concurrent file-backed creation can fail startup/search with index-lock/already-exists errors instead of sharing the one in-progress build as the old whole-build lock effectively did.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu.RLock. With BuildIndex now inserting into b.cache from many concurrent init workers and from lazy getOrCreateIndex builds, that unlocked iteration can race with a concurrent map write, which is a data race and can cause a fatal Go runtime 'concurrent map iteration and map write' panic that crashes the process. TotalDocs should snapshot or iterate under RLock (taking care not to hold it while calling out if that can re-enter).

findings.title: init errgroup goroutines race on shared err and totalBatchesIndexed
findings.body: Inside searchSupport.init, each errgroup goroutine executes totalBatchesIndexed++ and assigns to the outer err variable captured from 'stats, err := ...' via '_, _, err = s.build(...)'. With SetLimit(initWorkers) running builds concurrently this is a data race: increments can be lost (wrong 'namespaced_indexed' span attribute) and per-namespace build errors can overwrite each other before 'return err', masking a failed namespace build or reporting another namespace's error. Use a local err per goroutine and an atomic/mutex-protected counter.

findings.title: NewResourceServer performs uncancellable init with the server's background context
findings.body: NewResourceServer now synchronously calls s.Init(ctx) where ctx is the internally created context.Background()-derived watcher context (no caller context, deadline, or cancellation is accepted by the constructor). Building every search index can take arbitrarily long, and a caller that wants to abandon/shut down startup cannot cancel it and has no server handle yet on which to call Stop (which is the only place that cancels this ctx). Startup can thus hang indefinitely inside the constructor; previously a slow/failed init surfaced on the first RPC with that RPC's cancellable context.

findings.title: History and Origin panic when search is not configured
findings.body: When opts.Search.Resources is nil (or the search backend is nil) NewResourceServer leaves s.search nil, yet History (line 925) and Origin (line 930) unconditionally dereference s.search, unlike Search which returns 'search index not configured'. After this PR removed the per-RPC Init guards, a History/Origin gRPC call to a server constructed without search will nil-pointer panic and crash the handler/process instead of returning an error.
